notes: Ran unchanged R&D several times per turn and facechecked remotes at 2-3 credits. Then sat on 20-29 credits clicking for credits while the corp advanced and scored two agendas behind a single Hagen that Black Orchestra could break.

Scoring plan was sound (Biotic Labor fast-advance, iced remotes), but it built several empty iced remotes and clicked for credits at 20+ while discarding from a full HQ. It also installed Hyperloop with no advancement against a 38-credit runner, and that agenda was stolen.
After a decent opening it stopped running entirely and clicked for credits from turn 5 to turn 13, ending at 52 credits. The corp advanced and scored three agendas from one remote unchallenged.

The Tollbooth rez blocked Account Siphon and the agendas were scored steadily. It also iced empty remotes, click-drew into forced discards, and left an agenda (later GFI) naked in a remote for a turn while nearly broke.

Good reads: it ran the cash-starved corp's 3-ice remote twice for two steals, then kept steady Aumakua R&D pressure to win. Early facechecks at 5 and 1 credits cost a click and a core damage that trashing Street Peddler could have avoided.

The IP Block lock left the runner broke and tagged, but the corp clicked for credits from turn 4 to turn 16 (reaching 27 credits) without installing an agenda. It discarded agendas each turn into an open Archives, where Project Beale was stolen. Psychographics and Exchange of Information were played for no effect.

Smart plan: it stayed tagged to use Data Leak Reversal, milled R&D and stole three agendas from Archives. Minor waste included facechecking Cobra on 1 credit, a second Paparazzi, and installing Daily Casts while heavily tagged.

After taking Snare it was tagged on a tiny grip against a rich Weyland, yet it drew instead of clearing the tag and re-ran R&D into the same known Snare. That left 0 cards and a guaranteed Scorched Earth flatline.

It built a well-iced scoring remote and won, but sat at 0-3 credits most of the game while never installing the Melange Mining Corp it held. It spent its last credits trashing low-value resources and forfeited Posted Bounty for a tag it could not exploit.

The remote scoring and the Jeeves fast-advance finish were fine, but HQ was never iced in 16 turns. The runner hit it four times a turn and stole Hostile Takeover and GFI, while the corp clicked for credits at 16-20.
It never iced R&D while a 1-credit runner ran it four times every turn, and spent five turns clicking for credits and playing IPO up to 30 credits. It lost to agendas stolen off the top of R&D.

It made good steals on turn 7 and eventually won on R&D, but it ran the same Marilyn Campaign remote five times without trashing it. It let a fresh 2-advancement agenda in Server 3 be scored, and wasted Mad Dash for meat damage on an empty Archives.

It clicked for credits from turn 4 to 9 at 15-24 credits while discarding. It then put two agendas in a Vanilla-only remote that was stolen twice, even though a 4-ice remote stood empty, and the last agenda was stolen from Archives.

It hoarded 30-43 credits clicking for credits for most of the game without installing its held programs and resources, and made repeated pointless Yagura runs that it jacked out of. At 6 points against Jinteki it ran into Komainu with a full grip and ignored the new remote, so the Philotic Entanglement flatline was foreseeable.

It re-ran the same known Urtica Cipher remote four times, taking 3 net damage each time and losing Unity and Cleaver, sometimes paying 11 credits to get in. Meanwhile the corp scored three agendas from the other remote uncontested.

Every agenda after the first went into a fresh naked remote, so three Fetal AIs and a Gila Hands were stolen. Meanwhile a 3-ice remote it built stayed empty all game, and many turns were spent clicking for credits.

It went long stretches passive (turns 4-8 and 15-16) clicking for credits while the corp built and scored from its remote. Fisk Investment Seminar fed the corp cards, and it made a futile repeat run into the known Tollbooth.
Hansei Review trashed Obokata Protocol into an open Archives on turn 1, gifting 3 points. Otherwise the 2-ice remote scored steadily, with some idle credit-clicking at 16-21 credits.

Solid tempo: Retribution removed the breaker, Seamless Launch helped, and it scored repeatedly from one remote. It left R&D open early and put Offworld Office in a fresh single-ice remote that was stolen.

The strong opening R&D pressure included many repeat runs on an unchanged R&D top card. At 5 points it then clicked for credits from turn 11 to 15 (reaching 33 credits) while the corp scored four agendas through one Enigma, without drawing for breakers or building Aumakua counters.
